web_evidence.title: I, Alex Cross — Penguin sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized publisher sample sustains third-person narration in the prologue, switches to Alex's first-person narration in Chapters 1–4, and returns to third person for Gabriel Reese in Chapter 5.

web_evidence.title: I, Alex Cross by James Patterson — Excerpt
web_evidence.note: This excerpt, reprinted with Vision's permission, independently displays the same opening structure: third-person prologue sections, first-person Alex chapters, and a sustained third-person Gabriel Reese chapter.

search_log: Searched “I, Alex Cross” James Patterson excerpt, first chapter, publisher sample, and author-site combinations.
Searched the exact title with “first person,” “third-person,” “point of view,” “narrator,” and “alternating perspectives.”
Opened the Penguin publisher sample and verified third-person prologue material, first-person Chapter 1, and third-person Chapter 5.
Opened the Bookreporter excerpt and verified that it reproduces the prologue through Chapter 7 with permission from Vision.
Checked Google Books, Publishers Weekly, Bookreporter's review, and AudioFile; these confirmed the edition or plot but did not explicitly establish whole-book narrative person.
A general Alex Cross series description reported the usual first-person/third-person pattern, but it was not relied upon as book-specific structural evidence.
person_note: The quotes diagnostically corroborate Alex Cross's participating first-person narration, while the authorized opening excerpts show sustained third-person sections both before and among Alex's first-person chapters. Those autonomous third-person sections are base narrative rather than speech, thought, or embedded documents, so the correct label is ALTERNATING. Confidence is medium because the two strong web sources reproduce substantially the same opening material, the Goodreads quotes expose only the first-person strand, and no independent whole-book structural analysis was found.
